sentences.text: Eschatornis aterradora, meaning 'last terrifying bird,' is known from a single partial left tibiotarsus — a leg bone combining the tibia and tarsus.
Its shape matches the family Phorusrhacidae, or terror birds, specifically resembling the subfamilies Psilopterinae and Mesembriornithinae.
The holotype specimen MCL-A-1.795 — the specimen the species is based on — was found by Cástor Cartelle in the Toca dos Ossos cave in Bahia, Brazil, and formally described in 2026.
While initially thought to be an indeterminate cathartid in 2008, features like an oblique supratendinal bridge and an oval opening on the extensor sulcus now link it firmly to phorusrhacids.
Living between 25,326 and 25,733 calibrated years Before Present, it may have extended the known range of terror birds into the Late Pleistocene within a mesic, arboreal savannah.
